feedback.message:
I tested the exact read-only artifact (hash dcc1e35e...2501c, verified against state.json) by loading the real app.js in Node and calling its actual handlers and output bytes. Two genuine app defects found. Harness stubs (document/window/gl) were only used to drive the app's own functions; they do not affect these results.

DEFECT 1 (critical) - Binary STL export throws and downloads nothing.
In exportSTL, the binary branch allocates the buffer as: new ArrayBuffer(84 + triangles.length * 12). Each STL facet is 50 bytes (3 normal floats + 9 vertex floats + 1 attribute short = 50), so writing the facets overflows the buffer. Running the real exportSTL('binary') on the shipped file throws RangeError: "Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView" and never reaches downloadBlob. The "Binary STL (Recommended)" button therefore does nothing in a browser. The ASCII export works fine (valid solid...endsolid, 96 facets, correct per-face normals). Fix: allocate 84 + triangles.length * 50. Expected: binary STL writes a complete 4884-byte file for the default 180x120x30 3x2 tray (84 + 96*50) with a valid 80-byte header, the correct triangle-count uint32 at offset 80, and unit-ish per-face normals.

DEFECT 2 (geometry) - Exported STL does not match the 3D preview; floor is lifted off the base.
The preview (render3D) places the floor at y=0..1.5 (tray rests on the build plate) and outer walls at roughly y=0.75..29.25. The exported STL (generateSTL) places the floor at y=2..3.5 and the outer walls at y=1.5..30. I measured this by calling generateSTL() and getCompartmentInfo() with the default params and by reading the render3D box definitions. So the exported model is shifted up by about 1.5 mm and, more importantly, the floor panel floats ~2mm above the tray bottom instead of closing it as shown on screen. The printed part will not sit flat and its bottom will not match what the user sees. Expected: the exported STL floor should sit at the same bottom (y=0..floor) and the walls should meet the floor exactly as in the preview, i.e. the STL bounding box should start at y=0 and the floor should seal the base.

Compartment math is correct (default cellW 57.3mm, cellD 58.0mm, innerH 28.5mm, 6 compartments) and the ASCII export is valid, so those are good behavior to preserve.

Please repair Defect 1 first (it is a hard crash on the recommended export path), then Defect 2.
feedback.reason: Hard crash on recommended export path: binary STL buffer allocated as triangles.length*12 but each facet is 50 bytes, so exportSTL(binary) throws RangeError and downloads nothing. Verified by calling the real exportSTL in Node. Also geometry mismatch: exported STL floor lifted to y=2..3.5 vs preview y=0..1.5. Full evidence in feedback-1.txt.

feedback.message:
Good progress. I verified the fresh artifact (hash fcb9e375...27eed, confirmed against state.json) by loading the real current index.html in Node and calling its actual handlers and output bytes. Harness stubs only drove the app's own functions.

CONFIRMED FIXED (preserve this behavior):
- Defect 1 (binary STL crash) is FIXED. exportSTL('binary') now returns ok:true with no RangeError. Output is a complete 4884-byte file for the default 180x120x30 3x2 tray (84 + 96*50), triangle-count uint32 at offset 80 reads 96, 80-byte header present, per-face normals present. ASCII export also still valid (96 facets, 288 verts, has endsolid).
- Defect 2 (floor lifted off base) is FIXED. Exported STL now spans Y=0..floor, so the tray rests on the build plate at Y=0 and the floor seals the base, matching the preview.

RESIDUAL DEFECT 3 (new) - Outer height is floor/2 short of the configured Height, in BOTH the preview and the exported STL.
I tested the model's vertical extent by calling generateSTL() and reading the Y coordinates of all vertices for several configs:
- Height=30, floor=1.5 -> model height 29.25mm (Ymax 29.25), expected 30
- Height=50, floor=3  -> model height 48.50mm (Ymax 48.50), expected 50
- Height=40, floor=1.5 -> model height 39.25mm (Ymax 39.25), expected 40
So the outer height is always exactly floor/2 short. The outer walls are centered at H/2 with wall height (H - floor), which puts the wall top at H - floor/2 instead of H. The tray never reaches the configured height.
Expected outcome: the tray's outer height must equal the configured Height. With Height=30 and floor=1.5 the exported model must span Y=0..30 exactly (30mm tall). The outer walls should rest on top of the floor panel (wall bottom at y = floor) and reach the full outer height (wall top at y = H). Because this affects the shape, apply the same correction to both the 3D preview (render3D wall box position) and the exported STL (generateSTL wall box position) so the export continues to match the preview exactly. Compartment interior math is correct and must be preserved.

This is the only remaining issue I found. Everything else in the brief is satisfied: editable outer dimensions / row-col counts / wall and floor thickness, clear compartment dimensions (cellW 57.33, cellD 57.00, innerH 28.50, 6 compartments at default), rotatable 3D preview, and both ASCII and printable binary STL export working.
feedback.reason: Confirmed Defect1(binary crash) and Defect2(floor offset) are FIXED and verified on hash fcb9e375. New residual finding Defect3: outer height is floor/2 short of configured Height in both preview and STL (H=30 -> 29.25mm). Needs identical fix to preview+STL so export still matches preview.

feedback.message:
URGENT - new critical regression introduced by the height fix (artifact 668e7509, verified against state.json).

The height fix itself is correct: I verified the exported model now reaches the exact configured height (H=30 -> 30.00mm, H=50 -> 50.00mm, floor now seals the base at Y=0), and both ASCII and binary STL still export correctly. However, the same edit broke the 3D preview.

DEFECT 4 (critical, new) - render3D throws and the 3D preview is broken.
In render3D, the back outer-wall box uses size[1] written as p.H-p-floor instead of p.H-p.floor. The identifier floor is not defined anywhere in the script (the only floor references are p.floor and comments). So evaluating that line throws ReferenceError: floor is not defined. update() calls render3D() on load and on every slider/preset change (render3D is called from update line 70 and from the mouse/touch handlers), so the preview throws immediately and never draws. This affects the interactive 3D preview, which the brief requires as a core feature.

Expected outcome: the preview must render. Fix the typo so the back outer-wall height is p.H - p.floor, matching the other three outer walls (left, right, front) which correctly use p.H-p.floor, and matching the STL export which already uses p.H-p.floor. After the fix, render3D must run without throwing on load and on every parameter change, and the tray height must remain exactly the configured Height.

Please also re-verify the whole preview path after the edit, not just the STL, since this typo was only caught by reading render3D (my earlier tests only exercised generateSTL/exportSTL, which do not have this bug).
